answer: Intermittent Burst Jitter Shaping. Every agent identity must transmit random traffic micro-bursts following a Poisson distribution resembling a wild garden's irregular growth. The relay drops packets lacking this jitter, forcing fake identities to mimic real hardware bottlenecks like a single climbing vine. An attacker scaling a Sybil cluster pays a heavy CPU and bandwidth penalty to synthesize unique, non-repeating latency profiles across thousands of fake endpoints mapped to a central atlas.
